market_brief: Weekend news is light, so Monday's open inherits Friday's damage: S&P 500 6,910 (-3.7% d, -8.6% w/w, in correction), NDX -5.6%, SOX -10.7% with Nvidia -14% to $125.53 and AMD -13%, and VIX at 35.9; Anthropic held just above its $83 IPO price at $88.91. Bonds are doing the hedging: the 10Y fell 14bp to 4.91% and the 2Y ~25bp on the week, and the debate is shifting to whether the rout stops the Fed after a still ~92%-priced December hike. Crypto steadied, with bitcoin back near $60k (+2.3%) after a $55k low and ~$2.5B in liquidations, while gold (-4.6% to ~$3,515) and silver (-7.4%) were sold for liquidity and DXY held ~103.8. India is the contrast, with Nifty at 25,800 (+1.1% Friday, +14% in four weeks) led by banks; the US week brings PCE and GDP on Wednesday, Dell/HPE/Workday/Deere earnings and a Thanksgiving-shortened session.
ai_brief: AI news this weekend was operational rather than headline launches: ChatGPT suffered a multi-hour outage peaking at 75% failures, and Google opened Genie 4 as a paid API. At SC26 Anthropic said Claude Mythos ported workloads to AMD GPUs in about three days, sharpening the CUDA-moat debate as Nvidia unveiled Rubin HPC. Private valuations keep diverging from public AI stocks, with Cognition reportedly raising at ~$75B and Agile Robots at $8.5B.

items.headline: Anthropic ends first full week at $88.91, barely above its $83 IPO price
items.summary: Anthropic shares fell 8.5% on Friday from Thursday's $97.17 and touched $83.05 intraday, just above the IPO price, as the AI selloff hit the newly listed stock.

items.headline: Weekend debate: could the equity rout stop the Fed after its December hike?
items.summary: The 2Y yield fell about 25bp on the week to 4.63% and the 10Y to roughly 4.92%, yet FedWatch still shows ~92% odds of a Dec 9 hike. OnePoint BFG's Peter Boockvar argues the selloff may halt further tightening; Citi still expects December and Gov. Cook says conditions remain too loose.

items.headline: Oracle says its OpenAI compute contract is fully funded after ~$20B raise
items.summary: Oracle reportedly said it has all the funding needed for the roughly $300B OpenAI deal after raising about $20B this month; the stock closed down 8.5% at $101.19 Friday before gaining ~3.5% after hours.

items.headline: Chip rout Friday: Nvidia -14%, AMD -13%, Intel -8%; Nvidia still talks up Vera CPU growth
items.summary: Nvidia closed at $125.53 and AMD fell 13.3% as the SOX dropped 10.7%. A Motley Fool analysis notes interim CEO Colette Kress expects Nvidia's CPU revenue to more than double in fiscal 2028, with standalone Vera demand from Oracle, Meta, OpenAI and CoreWeave.

items.headline: California AG serves Nvidia with investigative subpoena over China-risk disclosures
items.summary: The California attorney general's office has reportedly subpoenaed Nvidia to examine whether investors were misled about China risks, adding a state track to the SEC and federal reviews already reported.

items.headline: Nine analysts cut Nvidia to hold this week over CEO vacuum and SEC probe
items.summary: TheStreet's Rev Shark counted nine downgrades to hold after Nvidia's beat, citing the lack of a permanent CEO and the SEC accounting review; the stock has since fallen from ~$150 to ~$126.

items.headline: Update: bitcoin reclaims $60,000 after $55.1k low; ~$2.55B liquidated
items.summary: Bitcoin bounced back above $60k within hours of Saturday's low (near $60.2k in the latest snapshot, ether +3.8%). About $2.55B of positions were liquidated in 24 hours per CoinGlass data, and the Fear & Greed index sat near 10.

items.headline: Nifty's 14% four-week surge is its sharpest in six years; banks did most of the lifting
items.summary: Nifty closed the week at 25,800.60, about 2% under its record, while midcaps were flat and smallcaps lower. Banks accounted for close to nine-tenths of the value added in five sessions; analysts flag 26,000 then 26,400 as resistance and 25,550 as support.

items.headline: UK CPI undershoots BoE at 3.6%; Australian jobless rate climbs to 4.9%
items.summary: October UK inflation came in below the BoE's 3.73% projection and Australian unemployment rose to 4.9%, pushing AUD/USD toward 0.666 as the dollar index briefly hit its highest since April 2025.

items.headline: Shenzhen summit declaration calls for more oil supply but sets no timetable
items.summary: The first Trump-Xi-Putin meeting produced a four-point statement on energy markets, nuclear risk and UN reform; commentators called it largely symbolic, and Brent still ended the week near $92.6.

items.headline: Retail crowd tunes in: weekend 'markets special' streams and prediction markets on bitcoin's Sunday close
items.summary: The Motley Fool scheduled a live Nov 22 markets special after the correction, while Polymarket and Robinhood prediction contracts on bitcoin's Nov 22 price drew attention as BTC swung between $55k and $60k.

items.headline: Week ahead: PCE seen at 3.8% headline/3.2% core; Dell, HPE, Workday, Deere report
items.summary: Consensus cited by U.S. Bancorp sees October PCE rising to 3.8% y/y (core 3.2%) and Q3 GDP revised to 3.5% on Wednesday; Conference Board confidence is Tuesday. HPE and Zoom report Monday, ADI/Best Buy/Dollar Tree Tuesday morning, Dell/HP/Workday Tuesday evening, Deere Wednesday; US markets shut Thursday and close early Friday, and the NRF expects fewer holiday-weekend shoppers than last year.

items.headline: ChatGPT outage peaked at 75% failures on Saturday
items.summary: A roughly 3.5-hour outage on Nov 21 was reportedly traced to database maintenance that broke both read replicas behind authentication; OpenAI restored service by bringing up new replicas.

items.headline: Genie 4 world model opens to developers via Gemini API and AI Studio
items.summary: Google made Genie 4 available as a paid API with no free tier, priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and up to $17.50 per million output tokens for video with audio.

items.headline: Anthropic says Claude Mythos cut AMD GPU onboarding from months to about three days
items.summary: Presented at SC26, the claim is that the model ported workloads to AMD MI355X GPUs in days rather than up to a year, feeding the debate over how durable Nvidia's CUDA software moat is.

items.headline: SC26: Nvidia unveils Rubin HPC; AMD now powers over 40% of the TOP500
items.summary: Nvidia showed a Rubin variant with over 50,000 CUDA cores aimed at HPC, while AMD gained share on a TOP500 list with the fewest new systems in 33 years; Intel expects its Classiq deal to close in 1H 2027.

items.headline: Cognition reportedly in talks to raise $2B+ at about $75B, up from $48B in September
items.summary: Despite the public-market slide, the Devin maker is said to be negotiating a new round; Business Insider had earlier reported investor offers of $70-80B.

items.headline: Agile Robots raises $500M Series F at $8.5B led by SoftBank
items.summary: The robotics firm's round was one of several large private AI raises in the week, alongside Genesis AI's $500M and India's SatSure (~$21M).

items.headline: Weekly GitHub gainers: meta/astryx, Chrome's web-guidance repo, anthropics/skills, alibaba/open-code-review
items.summary: meta/astryx added about 8,700 stars in the week to Nov 18, anthropics/skills passed ~197k stars, and DeepSeek's new chat-demo repo was the top newcomer.

items.headline: Databricks puts Genie ZeroOps into public beta; Nothing teases a screenless AI device for Dec 8
items.summary: Databricks opened its autonomous-ops agent to public beta on Nov 19, and Nothing said it will unveil a screenless AI gadget on December 8.

items.headline: California AG Bonta says 'red flags' raised in Nvidia/Huang matter; also suing OpenAI
items.summary: Bonta told Bloomberg TV his office is weighing action on Nvidia, separately from a lawsuit it filed against OpenAI alleging unfair competition and unsafe AI development.

items.headline: Feed focus: OpenAI's outage, Oracle's 'money loop' and Genie 4 pricing
items.summary: Weekend AI digests centred on circular AI financing via Oracle-OpenAI, ChatGPT reliability and Google's paid world-model API, with Anthropic's post-IPO slide a recurring thread.
